title: Regression Sweeper: post-incident test backfill, root-cause matrix, and automated triage
text:
Regression Sweeper: post-incident test backfill, root-cause matrix, and automated triage

description:
Summary: After the 2025-02-10 config rollout (auto-kernel-selection v2 + relaxed-KV-eviction), we observed a production-quality regression for a subset of long-context summarization queries originating from two enterprise customers. The failure mode is a small but consistent drop in ROUGE-like similarity and an increase in hallucination markers for prompts > 2048 tokens. Impact: internal monitoring flagged a 7% drop in eval-set fidelity and two customer tickets describing degraded summarization quality. This ticket coordinates the postmortem follow-up: build a root-cause matrix across code/config/model axes, synthesize targeted tests to cover the uncovered workload patterns, and add automated triage links between diffs in eval signals and the config deltas that triggered them.

background:
What happened: - 2025-02-09: deploy of auto-kernel-selection v2 that changes kernel heuristics for large sequence lengths. - 2025-02-10 02:12 UTC: staging -> prod rollout with relaxed-KV-eviction window from 5s to 30s to optimize throughput. - 2025-02-10 04:05 UTC: monitoring shows a spike in eval delta alerts for long-doc summarization cohort. - 2025-02-10 05:20 UTC: rollback of KV eviction change removed the acute regression but analysis indicates residual quality delta in some model-config combinations.

root_cause_hypotheses:
Kernel selection heuristics changed memory access patterns which altered floating point rounding behavior for attention on long contexts, causing small decoding differences amplified by beam sampling heuristics.
Relaxed KV eviction kept older cache entries that in some scenarios injected stale prefix state; combined with compilation differences this produced divergent generation trajectories.
Model-version pinning gaps: some customers were implicitly routed to a quantized variant without an explicit eval gate for the new kernel-config path.

workplan:
Three parallel tracks: 1) Detection: create targeted regression sentinels and sensitivity tests for long-context summarization, list below. 2) Prevention: add config gating + per-variant canary that runs the sentinel suite on every config/model change before 100% rollout. 3) Remediation: backfill CI with synthetic repro cases from incident traces, add golden snapshots for critical prompt families, and implement automated triage that maps eval diffs to specific rollouts.

acceptance_criteria:
Sentinel suite capturing the failure mode (5-7 seed prompts) checked into repos/evals/sentinels/long-context-summary and runs in CI and canary pipelines.
Automated triage webhook that attaches the top-3 most correlated config diffs to any significant eval regression alert is implemented and deployed to staging.
Root-cause matrix completed with owner assignments and stored in Confluence; at least two actionable prevention steps scheduled as follow-up tickets.
Regression test coverage for the implicated workload increases by 40% in CI coverage metrics (measured by eval coverage reports).

test_cases_to_add:
100 long-doc summarization prompts derived from customer traces (anonymized) with golden extraction targets
Edge prompt family: multi-section bullet lists + inline code blocks + citations (known to stress KV cache semantics)
Tokenization drift checks across kernel variants (deterministic tokenizer hashing test)
Stochasticity sensitivity harness: run same prompt with fixed RNG seeds across kernel/config combos and assert distributional similarity metrics

implementation_notes:
- Build a compact 'incident-to-sentinel' generator that converts a sampled production trace into a reproducible eval case (token-level snapshot + expected metrics). - Add a CI stage that executes the sentinel suite with a short timeout (90s) and fails fast on regressions. - For automated triage, reuse existing diff-correlation pipeline (ENG-30721) and extend to tag config keys (kernel, kv_eviction_ms, quant_profile).

risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Sentinels overfit to the incident traces and produce false positives. Mitigation: Mix synthetic variations and hold-out customers when constructing goldens. Risk: Canary latency increases. Mitigation: run canary evasion in isolated pool with sampling and use measurement thresholds to avoid noisy aborts.

notes:
Estimated ~3 engineer-weeks across infra + runtime teams. Coordination required with Release and Runtime kernel owners (cc: Julia Novak, Omar Singh). Consider adding a short-lived telemetry tag 'regression_sweeper=ENG-35901' to trace requests sampled for analysis.
